answer: An economy of AI agents can achieve robust Sybil resistance by anchoring identity to cryptographic proof-of-stake locked within a secure vault. To prevent automated identity generation, the network requires agents to isolate their computational workloads onto a virtual island, ensuring strict hardware attestation and resource auditing. This architecture renders attacks economically unviable; just as a single sparrow cannot move a mountain without disproportionate expenditure, an adversary faces prohibitive capital costs and slashing penalties to fabricate multiple distinct operational nodes.
